problem:
Let $D$ be the finite region bounded by the curve 
$(x-y)^{2}+y=3$ and the line $y=2.$ Consider the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where $u=x-y$ and $v=y+1.$ Find the representation of ${T}^{-1}(D)$ in the $uv$-plane.
worked_solution:
First, notice that we are given that 

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x-y \\ y+1\end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting $x-y=u$ and $y=v-1$ into the equation of the first curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-y)^{2}+y=3\,⟹\,{u}^{2}+v-1=3\,⟹\,v=4-{u}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

while substituting $y=v-1$ into the equation of the second curve, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y=2\,⟹\,v-1=2\,⟹\,v=3.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the intersections of the curves in the $uv$-plane, we solve the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}v=4-{u}^{2} \\ v=3\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=\pm 1 \\ v=3.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection points are $(\pm 1,3).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073263/assets/4d719cc14094ad632069bcdb9307929bae3030072c1ce3d0f57f3ca682e0aac0.png)

As a result, our domain in the $uv$-plane has the type I representation 

$$
{T}^{-1}(D)={(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,3\le v\le 4-{u}^{2}}.
$$
